evidence.locator: PDF p. 3; 2 Development Process, first paragraph

qualifications: Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.

Subsequent paragraphs describe example datasheets, product teams, researcher/practitioner/policy comments and legal feedback; this is author-reported development, not a controlled effectiveness trial.

value.value: The questions and workflow were refined over roughly two years with multiple rounds of feedback.

evidence.locator: PDF p. 11; 4 Impact and Challenges, paragraph beginning Datasheets for datasets

qualifications: Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.
Creators cannot anticipate every use, demographic information may be unavailable, and documentation imposes time and organizational overhead.

value.value: The paper states that datasheets alone are not a complete mitigation for unwanted societal bias or potential dataset harms.

evidence.locator: PDF p. 3; 1.1 Objectives, final paragraph

qualifications: Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.
This is a normative framework design objective, not evidence that all later datasheet tools or datasets follow it.

value.value: The authors intend datasheet creation to involve reflective human documentation rather than an automated creation process.

evidence.locator: PDF p. 11; 4 Impact and Challenges, first full paragraph

qualifications: Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.
Dynamic datasets are identified as an implementation challenge. Dataset families and successive releases should retain separate documentation scope.

value.value: For infrequently changing datasets, the authors recommend accompanying updated dataset versions with updated datasheets.

evidence.locator: PDF p. 7; 3.3 Collection Process, fourth bullet

qualifications: Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.
This is a recommended disclosure question. It does not establish participation, fair payment or a particular supplier contract for any dataset.

value.value: The proposed collection-process documentation asks dataset creators to identify collection participants and their compensation.

evidence.locator: PDF p. 4; 4 Direct Preference Optimization, opening paragraph

qualifications: Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.
The equivalence uses the paper’s KL-constrained objective and preference-model assumptions. Preference-labelled pairs are still required.

value.value: DPO fits an implicit reward through a direct policy objective without fitting a separate reward model and running an RL training loop.

evidence.locator: PDF p. 7; 6 Experiments / Tasks, summarization paragraph

qualifications: Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.
The tested SFT model differs from the one used to collect the preferences. This paper establishes reuse, not a newly commissioned annotation supplier contribution.

value.value: The summarization experiment reuses human preference annotations collected by Stiennon et al.

evidence.locator: PDF p. 7; 6 Experiments / Tasks, controlled sentiment paragraph

qualifications: Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.
These labels are model-generated for a controlled experiment, rather than human preference annotations; the paper calls the classifier the ground-truth reward for this setup.

value.value: The controlled IMDb sentiment experiment generates preference pairs using a pretrained sentiment classifier.

evidence.locator: PDF p. 10; 7 Discussion / Limitations & Future Work

qualifications: Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.
Larger-model scaling, broader distribution shift, reward over-optimization and automated judge prompting are left for further study; no universal PPO-superiority claim follows.
